# Research Brief — rame-studio

**Project:** rame-studio  
**Slug:** rame-studio  
**Status:** done  
**Last updated:** 2026-10-27  
**Owner:** Research Agent  
**Approved inputs:** docs/plan/PLAN.md (v3, approved), docs/design/DESIGN.md (locked)

---

## 1. Product context

Rame Studio is a studio & project management SaaS for creative teams. Core scope: multi-tenant workspaces, projects, tasks, time tracking, real-time chat, file assets, invoicing/payments (Stripe), bilingual UI (fa/en) with RTL support, JWT authentication, ASP.NET Core 10 Web API + EF Core 10 + PostgreSQL backend, React 19 + Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + Antigravity UI frontend.

---

## 2. Competitor / similar product analysis

| Product | Category | Strengths | Weaknesses vs. rame-studio | Differentiation for rame-studio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Monday.com** | Work OS / project management | Highly visual, strong automations, broad integrations, mature mobile apps | Expensive at scale, complex pricing tiers, RTL/i18n is secondary, real-time chat is limited | Bilingual fa/en RTL-first design, integrated Stripe invoicing, SignalR real-time chat, simpler flat pricing for creative studios |
| **Asana** | Task & project management | Clean UX, strong task dependencies, good portfolio views | No built-in payments/invoicing, weak real-time collaboration, limited RTL support | Native Stripe billing, real-time chat via SignalR, RTL layout for Persian/Arabic users |
| **ClickUp** | All-in-one PM | Feature-dense (docs, goals, time tracking), generous free tier | Overwhelming UI, steep learning curve, performance issues at scale, RTL not a priority | Focused creative-studio scope, cleaner UX, RTL-first, integrated payments |
| **Notion** | Docs + databases + PM | Flexible blocks, strong docs/wiki, good i18n | No real-time chat, weak project tracking, no native payments, RTL support is limited | Purpose-built project management, SignalR chat, Stripe invoicing, RTL layout |
| **Trello** | Kanban PM | Simple, intuitive, Power-Ups | Limited reporting, no native invoicing, weak RTL, basic real-time | Full project management + invoicing + RTL, not just kanban |
| **Jira** | Software project management | Powerful agile tooling, deep integrations | Enterprise-focused, complex, expensive, poor RTL, no built-in payments | Creative-studio oriented, simpler, Stripe-native, RTL-first |

**Key takeaway:** rame-studio's differentiators are (a) RTL-first fa/en i18n, (b) integrated Stripe payments/invoicing, (c) real-time chat via SignalR, and (d) a focused creative-studio feature set rather than enterprise bloat.

---

## 3. Stack validation

| Layer | Choice | Validation |
|---|---|---|
| **Backend framework** | ASP.NET Core 10 Web API | .NET 10 is the current LTS (released Nov 2025), supported through Nov 2027. Minimal APIs + controllers, built-in JWT bearer, SignalR, OpenAPI support. |
| **ORM / data access** | EF Core 10 | EF Core 10 ships with .NET 10, supports PostgreSQL via Npgsql, complex types, raw SQL, and migrations. Mature, well-documented. |
| **Database** | PostgreSQL | Production-grade relational DB, strong JSONB support (useful for flexible asset metadata), excellent Npgsql driver, widely hosted (RDS, Azure, Docker). |
| **Identity / auth** | ASP.NET Core Identity + JWT | Built-in Identity with EF Core stores, JWT bearer middleware, refresh-token pattern well-established. |
| **Frontend framework** | React 19 | React 19 (released late 2024) with Actions, improved hydration, better asset loading. Stable and widely adopted. |
| **Build tool** | Vite | Fast dev server, HMR, optimized builds, TypeScript-native, React plugin mature. |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS | Utility-first, JIT compiler, dark mode, RTL via `rtlcss` or logical properties, Antigravity UI built on Tailwind. |
| **UI component library** | Antigravity UI | Tailwind-based React component kit; DESIGN.md is locked to this choice. Verify component coverage (tables, forms, modals, charts) before build. |
| **Type safety** | TypeScript | Strict mode, shared DTO contracts via OpenAPI client generation. |
| **Real-time** | SignalR | ASP.NET Core SignalR with WebSocket transport, JS client `@microsoft/signalr`, automatic fallback to SSE/long polling. |
| **Payments** | Stripe | Stripe .NET SDK + Stripe.js on frontend, webhooks for async events, PCI scope reduced via Payment Elements. |
| **API docs** | Swashbuckle / Swagger | OpenAPI 3 generation, XML comments, endpoint filtering, used for frontend client generation. |
| **Object mapping** | Mapster | Fast, convention-based DTO↔entity mapping, compiled projections, low overhead vs AutoMapper. |
| **PostgreSQL driver** | Npgsql | Official EF Core provider for PostgreSQL, supports JSONB, arrays, range types, batching. |
| **i18n** | react-i18next | Mature React i18n library, namespaces, interpolation, pluralization, RTL direction switching. |
| **Routing** | react-router-dom | Declarative routing, loaders/actions (v6+), nested routes, protected route wrappers. |
| **Design tokens** | Vitrea tokens | Token-based theming (colors, spacing, typography) consumed by Tailwind config and Antigravity UI. |

**Validation result:** The stack is coherent, all components are production-ready as of 2026-10-27, and there are no known version conflicts between .NET 10, EF Core 10, React 19, Vite, and Tailwind. Antigravity UI is the one external dependency to verify for component completeness.

---

## 4. Key libraries & APIs

### Backend (.NET 10)
- **ASP.NET Core 10** — Web API, minimal APIs, controllers, middleware pipeline.
- **EF Core 10** — ORM, migrations, change tracking, complex types, raw SQL.
- **Npgsql** — PostgreSQL provider for EF Core, JSONB/array support.
- **ASP.NET Core Identity** — user management, roles, password hashing, EF Core stores.
- **Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.JwtBearer** — JWT validation, token issuance.
- **Mapster / MapsterMapper** — DTO↔entity mapping, compiled projections.
- **Swashbuckle.AspNetCore** — OpenAPI/Swagger generation, UI, XML doc integration.
- **Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR** — hubs, client connections, groups, presence.
- **Stripe.net** — official Stripe .NET SDK (customers, payment intents, subscriptions, webhooks).
- **Serilog / Microsoft.Extensions.Logging** — structured logging.
- **FluentValidation** — request validation (if used per DESIGN.md).

### Frontend (React 19 + Vite + TypeScript)
- **React 19** — UI framework, Actions, hooks.
- **Vite** — dev server, HMR, build, TypeScript support.
- **TypeScript** — strict type checking.
- **Tailwind CSS** — utility-first styling, JIT, dark mode.
- **Antigravity UI** — Tailwind-based React component library (locked by DESIGN.md).
- **react-router-dom** — client-side routing, protected routes, nested layouts.
- **react-i18next** — translation, namespaces, language switching (fa/en).
- **@microsoft/signalr** — SignalR JS client for real-time chat.
- **@stripe/stripe-js / @stripe/react-stripe-js** — Stripe Elements, Payment Element.
- **Vitrea tokens** — design tokens (colors, spacing, typography) consumed via Tailwind config.
- **Axios / fetch** — API client with JWT interceptor.
- **Vitest / React Testing Library** — unit and component testing.

---

## 5. Risk register

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Authentication / JWT security** | Medium | High | Short-lived access tokens + refresh tokens in HttpOnly cookies, HTTPS only, token revocation list, rate limiting on auth endpoints, Identity lockout policy. |
| **Payments (Stripe)** | Medium | High | Use Stripe Payment Elements (PCI SAQ A), verify webhook signatures, idempotency keys, test in Stripe test mode only (no real money spent), retry logic for failed payments. |
| **Real-time chat (SignalR)** | Medium | Medium | WebSocket-first with SSE fallback, connection limits per user, message size limits, reconnection logic, presence tracking, scale-out with Redis backplane if needed. |
| **RTL layout (fa/en)** | Medium | Medium | CSS logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`), `dir="rtl"` on `<html>`, test both directions, mirror icons/images, Antigravity UI RTL support verification. |
| **Deployment** | Medium | Medium | Docker multi-stage builds, docker-compose for local parity, CI/CD pipeline, environment variable validation, database migrations as separate step, blue/green or rolling updates, health checks. |
| **Antigravity UI component gaps** | Medium | Medium | Audit component coverage against DESIGN.md before build; prepare fallback/custom components or alternative Tailwind kit. |
| **EF Core 10 / Npgsql version alignment** | Low | Medium | Pin exact versions, test migrations locally, avoid preview packages. |
| **React 19 breaking changes** | Low | Medium | Review React 19 migration guide, test Actions and hydration behavior, lock React version. |

---

## 6. Open questions

1. Does Antigravity UI provide all components needed (data tables, date pickers, charts, file upload)? If not, what is the fallback Tailwind component kit?
2. Is Vitrea tokens a published npm package or an internal design-token set? How is it consumed in Tailwind config?
3. What is the SignalR scale-out strategy (Redis backplane) for multi-server deployment?
4. Are Stripe webhooks handled via dedicated controller endpoints with signature verification?
5. What is the refresh-token storage and rotation strategy?

---

## 7. Acceptance criteria (verified)

- [x] Competitor/similar product analysis (studio & project management SaaS) — Section 2
- [x] Stack validation (.NET 10 + EF Core 10 + PostgreSQL + React 19 + Vite + Tailwind + Antigravity UI) — Section 3
- [x] Key libraries & APIs (Mapster, Npgsql, Swashbuckle, Stripe, SignalR, react-i18next, react-router-dom, Vitrea tokens) — Section 4
- [x] Risk register with mitigation (auth, payments, real-time chat, RTL layout, deployment) — Section 5

**Status:** done — BRIEF.md refreshed, no money spent, no publishing performed.

# Marketing Strategy — Rame Studio

**Project:** rame-studio  
**Slug:** rame-studio  
**Date:** 2026-10-27  
**Owner:** Marketing Agent  
**Status:** Draft (for review)

---

## 1. Positioning Statement & Target Audience

### 1.1 Positioning Statement

**Rame Studio** is the first studio-management platform built from the ground up for bilingual (Persian/English) RTL studios. While general scheduling tools treat right-to-left languages as an afterthought, Rame Studio delivers a native fa/en RTL experience across admin, customer, and team dashboards — with JWT-secured auth, real-time SignalR chat, and Stripe payments — so Persian-speaking studios can run bookings, classes, and client communication in their own language without compromise.

**For:** Independent studios, salons, spas, fitness/yoga studios, and creative studios in Persian-speaking markets (Iran, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, diaspora) plus bilingual studios serving mixed fa/en clientele.

**Who need:** appointment booking, class scheduling, client management, team coordination, in-chat communication, and online payments — all in a single RTL-native platform.

**Unlike:** Mindbody, Vagaro, Booksy, Fresha, Acuity Scheduling, Square Appointments, Timely, Treatwell, StyleSeat — which are English-first and offer weak or no RTL support.

**Rame Studio is:** the RTL-native studio operating system that lets Persian-speaking studios book, manage, chat, and get paid in their own language.

### 1.2 Target Audience

| Segment | Profile | Pain Points | Why Rame Studio |
|---------|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Boutique studios (salons, spas, nail bars)** | 1–10 staff, Persian-speaking, owner-operated | No RTL booking tool; English-only platforms feel foreign; WhatsApp/Telegram chat fragmented | Native fa RTL booking page + in-app SignalR chat replaces WhatsApp chaos |
| **Fitness & yoga studios** | 5–25 staff, class-based, mixed fa/en clientele | Class scheduling in Persian is clunky on English platforms; payments fragmented | RTL class schedule + Stripe payments + team dashboard |
| **Creative studios (photo, design, tattoo)** | 1–8 staff, appointment-based, portfolio-driven | No client portal in Persian; booking links look unprofessional | Branded fa/en customer dashboard with portfolio + booking |
| **Diaspora studios (outside Iran)** | Persian-speaking owners serving local + expat clients | Need bilingual fa/en interface; existing tools are English-only | Dual-language fa/en UI with RTL/LTR switching |

### 1.3 Primary ICP (Ideal Customer Profile)

- **Location:** Iran, Afghanistan, Tajikistan, UAE (Dubai Persian community), Turkey (Istanbul), Los Angeles (Tehrangeles), Toronto, London
- **Business size:** 1–25 staff, solo to small studio
- **Monthly bookings:** 50–2,000
- **Tech comfort:** Uses WhatsApp/Telegram for bookings today; wants to move to a professional platform
- **Language:** Persian-first, English-second (bilingual staff)

### 1.4 Positioning Pillars

1. **RTL-native:** Built for Persian/Arabic script from day one, not translated after the fact.
2. **All-in-one:** Booking + chat + payments + team + customer dashboards in one platform.
3. **Bilingual:** Seamless fa/en switching for staff and customers.
4. **Modern stack:** .NET 10 backend, React 19 frontend, SignalR real-time, Stripe payments — fast, secure, scalable.

---

## 2. Launch Strategy

### 2.1 Launch Phases

| Phase | Goal | Timeline | Channels | Exit Criteria |
|-------|------|----------|----------|---------------|
| **P1 — Private Beta** | Validate core booking + chat with 10–15 design partners | Weeks 1–4 | Direct outreach, WhatsApp/Telegram studio groups, founder network | 10 active studios, 100+ bookings, NPS ≥ 40 |
| **P2 — Public Beta (fa)** | Open registration for Persian-speaking studios | Weeks 5–8 | Persian product-hunt channels, Instagram/Telegram ads, studio associations | 50 registered studios, 500+ bookings, 20% conversion to paid |
| **P3 — Public Launch (fa/en)** | Full bilingual launch, Stripe payments live | Weeks 9–12 | Product Hunt, LinkedIn, SEO content, referral program | 100 paying studios, $5K MRR, 4.5+ app-store rating |
| **P4 — Growth** | Scale to regional markets, add features | Month 4+ | Paid acquisition, partnerships, content SEO | 250 paying studios, $15K MRR, <5% monthly churn |

### 2.2 Channels

**Organic (low cost, high trust):**
- **Telegram & WhatsApp studio groups** — where Persian studio owners already congregate; share demo videos in Persian
- **Instagram** — visual platform for salons/spas; Persian reels showing RTL booking flow
- **LinkedIn** — B2B outreach to studio associations and coaches
- **SEO content** — Persian-language blog: "بهترین نرم‌افزار مدیریت سالن" (best salon management software), RTL booking guides

**Paid (after beta validation):**
- **Instagram/Telegram ads** targeted to Persian-speaking studio owners in Iran, UAE, Turkey, LA, Toronto
- **Google Search ads** on Persian keywords: "رزرو نوبت سالن", "مدیریت رزرو سالن زیبایی"

**Partnerships:**
- Studio equipment suppliers (salon chairs, yoga mats) — co-marketing
- Persian business associations — newsletter mentions, webinars

**Product-led:**
- Free tier for up to 3 staff / 100 bookings/month
- Referral program: 1 month free for referrer + referee
- Embeddable "Book with Rame" widget for studio websites/Instagram bios

### 2.3 Launch Messaging (fa/en)

**English headline:** "Run your studio in Persian. Book, chat, get paid — all in one RTL-native platform."

**Persian headline:** "سالن خود را به فارسی مدیریت کنید. رزرو، چت و پرداخت — همه در یک پلتفرم RTL."

**Key proof points:**
- First studio platform with native fa/en RTL
- Real-time chat between staff and customers (SignalR)
- Stripe payments in local currency where supported
- Admin, customer, and team dashboards
- Free to start; pay as you grow

---

## 3. Measurable Growth Experiments

Each experiment runs for 2–4 weeks with a defined hypothesis, KPIs, and success threshold.

### Experiment 1: Persian WhatsApp/Telegram Direct Outreach

**Hypothesis:** Personalized Persian-language direct messages to studio owners in Telegram groups convert at ≥10% to beta signups.

**KPIs:** Messages sent, reply rate, beta signups, CAC
**Success threshold:** ≥10% signup rate, CAC < $5
**Owner:** Marketing
**Timeline:** Weeks 1–4 (P1)

### Experiment 2: Instagram Reels — RTL Booking Demo

**Hypothesis:** 30-second Persian reels showing the RTL booking flow generate ≥2× more profile visits than static posts.

**KPIs:** Reel views, profile visits, click-through to landing page, signups
**Success threshold:** ≥5,000 views per reel, ≥2% CTR to landing page
**Owner:** Marketing
**Timeline:** Weeks 3–8 (P1–P2)

### Experiment 3: Referral Program

**Hypothesis:** A "1 month free for you + 1 month free for friend" referral program drives ≥20% of new signups.

**KPIs:** Referral signups, % of total signups from referrals, referral CAC
**Success threshold:** ≥20% of signups from referrals, referral CAC < $3
**Owner:** Marketing + Product
**Timeline:** Weeks 6–12 (P2–P3)

### Experiment 4: Persian SEO Content

**Hypothesis:** Publishing 8 Persian-language articles targeting "مدیریت رزرو سالن" and related keywords drives ≥500 organic visitors/month by month 4.

**KPIs:** Organic sessions, keyword rankings, organic signups
**Success threshold:** ≥500 organic sessions/month, ≥5% organic signup conversion
**Owner:** Marketing
**Timeline:** Weeks 8–16 (P3–P4)

### Experiment 5: Free-to-Paid Conversion

**Hypothesis:** Converting free-tier studios to paid at $19/month after 30 days or 100 bookings yields ≥15% conversion.

**KPIs:** Free-to-paid conversion rate, MRR, ARPU
**Success threshold:** ≥15% conversion, ARPU ≥ $19
**Owner:** Marketing + Product
**Timeline:** Weeks 9–16 (P3–P4)

### Experiment 6: Studio Equipment Supplier Partnership

**Hypothesis:** Co-marketing with 3 Persian studio-equipment suppliers yields ≥30 qualified leads each.

**KPIs:** Leads per partner, lead-to-trial conversion, partner CAC
**Success threshold:** ≥30 leads/partner, ≥10% trial conversion
**Owner:** Marketing
**Timeline:** Weeks 10–16 (P3–P4)

### Experiment 7: Google Search Ads (Persian Keywords)

**Hypothesis:** Persian-language Google Search ads on booking-related keywords achieve CAC < $25.

**KPIs:** Impressions, CTR, cost per click, signups, CAC
**Success threshold:** CTR ≥ 3%, CAC < $25
**Owner:** Marketing
**Timeline:** Weeks 12–16 (P3–P4)

### 3.1 North Star Metric & KPIs

**North Star:** Weekly active studios (WAS) — studios with ≥1 booking or chat message in the past 7 days.

**Primary KPIs:**
- MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue)
- Active studios (WAU/MAU)
- Free-to-paid conversion rate
- Monthly churn rate
- NPS (Net Promoter Score)
- CAC (Customer Acquisition Cost)
- LTV (Lifetime Value)

**Success targets by end of P4 (Month 6):**
- 250 paying studios
- $15K MRR
- <5% monthly churn
- ≥15% free-to-paid conversion
- NPS ≥ 40

---

## 4. Competitive Differentiation

### 4.1 Competitive Landscape

| Competitor | Strengths | Weaknesses vs Rame Studio |
|------------|-----------|---------------------------|
| **Mindbody** | Large ecosystem, classes + appointments, established brand | English-first, no RTL, expensive ($129–$599/mo), complex for small studios |
| **Vagaro** | All-in-one (booking, POS, marketing), US-focused | English-first, no RTL, per-provider pricing adds up |
| **Booksy** | Marketplace discovery, easy setup | English-first, no RTL, commission-based pricing |
| **Fresha** | Free core platform, no monthly fee | English-first, no RTL, marketplace model competes with your clients |
| **Acuity Scheduling** | Simple scheduling, Squarespace-owned | English-first, no RTL, limited team/chat features |
| **Square Appointments** | Integrated payments, free tier | English-first, no RTL, US-centric |
| **Timely** | Clean UI, good for salons | English-first, no RTL, NZ/AU-focused |
| **Treatwell** | Marketplace discovery, Europe-focused | English-first, no RTL, commission-based |
| **StyleSeat** | Beauty-focused marketplace | English-first, no RTL, US-focused |

### 4.2 Rame Studio's Differentiators

| Differentiator | Rame Studio | Typical Competitors |
|----------------|-------------|---------------------|
| **Native RTL (fa/en)** | ✅ Built for Persian/Arabic from day one | ❌ English-first, RTL as afterthought or missing |
| **Bilingual UI** | ✅ Seamless fa/en switching | ❌ Single language (English) |
| **In-app real-time chat** | ✅ SignalR chat between staff & customers | ❌ Limited or no chat; rely on WhatsApp/email |
| **All-in-one dashboards** | ✅ Admin + customer + team | ⚠️ Often split across products |
| **Stripe payments** | ✅ Integrated, multi-currency | ✅ Available but often English-only checkout |
| **Modern stack** | ✅ .NET 10 + React 19 + SignalR | ⚠️ Mixed; often legacy PHP/monolith |
| **Persian market focus** | ✅ Built for Iran/Afghanistan/Tajikistan/diaspora | ❌ US/Europe-focused |

### 4.3 Positioning Against Key Competitors

**vs Mindbody:** "Mindbody is powerful but English-only and expensive. Rame Studio gives Persian studios the same all-in-one power — booking, chat, payments — in their own language, at a fraction of the cost."

**vs Vagaro/Booksy:** "Vagaro and Booksy are great for English-speaking salons but offer no RTL support. Rame Studio is built for Persian-speaking studios from the ground up."

**vs Fresha:** "Fresha is free but takes your customers through an English marketplace. Rame Studio keeps your brand and language front and center — no marketplace, no commission on bookings."

**vs Acuity/Square:** "Acuity and Square handle scheduling well but are English-only with no team chat. Rame Studio adds real-time SignalR chat and full Persian RTL."

### 4.4 Moat

1. **RTL-native UX** — hard to retrofit; competitors would need to rebuild their frontend for Persian/Arabic script.
2. **Bilingual fa/en** — serves a specific market segment competitors ignore.
3. **Real-time chat** — SignalR chat keeps communication in-platform, reducing WhatsApp fragmentation.
4. **Local market trust** — Persian-language support, local payment options, cultural fit.

---

## 5. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|------------|
| Sanctions/payment restrictions on Iran | Medium | High | Stripe may not work in Iran; target diaspora markets (UAE, Turkey, LA, Toronto) first; offer alternative payment gateways |
| Low adoption of new platform by WhatsApp-dependent studios | High | Medium | Free tier, concierge onboarding, migrate WhatsApp chats into SignalR |
| Competitors add RTL support | Low | Medium | First-mover advantage, local language support, community relationships |
| Technical: SignalR chat at scale | Low | Medium | Load test early, horizontal scaling on .NET 10 |

# Rame Studio — Operations Runbook

**Project:** rame-studio  
**Slug:** rame-studio  
**Stack:** .NET 10 Clean Architecture backend + React 19 / Vite frontend  
**Services:** api, frontend, postgres:16-alpine, redis  
**Orchestration:** Docker Compose  
**Database:** EF Core migrations + seed data  
**Date:** 2026-10-27  
**Owner:** Operations Agent  

---

## 1. Build & Deploy

### 1.1 Prerequisites

- Docker Engine ≥ 26
- Docker Compose (v2 plugin or standalone)
- .NET 10 SDK (for local `dotnet ef` commands outside containers)
- `docker compose` available on PATH

### 1.2 First-time deploy

```bash
# 1. Clone / enter the project
cd ~/Projects/devpilot/rame-studio

# 2. Copy environment file and review values
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env as needed (see Section 2)

# 3. Build all images
docker compose build

# 4. Start all services (detached)
docker compose up -d

# 5. Wait for the API to become healthy (see Section 3)
curl -s http://localhost:5000/health | head -c 200; echo

# 6. Apply EF Core migrations
docker compose exec api dotnet ef database update --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api

# 7. Run seed data (roles + test users + packages)
docker compose exec api dotnet run --project src/Api -- SeedData.InitializeAsync
```

> **Note:** The container entrypoint (`docker/entrypoint.sh`) already runs `wait-for-db.sh` before starting the API, so the API will not start until Postgres is reachable. Migrations and seeding are intentionally separate manual steps so you can inspect them before applying.

### 1.3 Routine redeploy (no schema change)

```bash
docker compose build
docker compose up -d
```

### 1.4 Redeploy with migration

```bash
docker compose build
docker compose up -d
docker compose exec api dotnet ef database update --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api
```

### 1.5 Stop / remove everything

```bash
docker compose down          # stops and removes containers, keeps volumes
docker compose down -v       # also removes named volumes (destroys DB data!)
```

---

## 2. Environment Variables Reference

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and adjust for your environment. Never commit `.env`.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` | `Development` | .NET environment name |
| `ASPNETCORE_URLS` | `http://+:5000` | API listening URLs |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `Host=db;Port=5432;Database=rame_studio;Username=postgres;Password=postgres` | Postgres connection string (also accepts `postgres://` URIs) |
| `POSTGRES_DB` | `rame_studio` | Postgres database name |
| `POSTGRES_USER` | `postgres` | Postgres admin user |
| `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | `postgres` | Postgres admin password |
| `PGDATA` | `/var/lib/postgresql/data` | Postgres data directory inside container |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://redis:6379` | Redis connection string |
| `Jwt:Secret` | `SuperSecretKeyForRameStudio2026JwtAuthMin32Chars!` | JWT signing key (change in production) |
| `Jwt:Issuer` | `RameStudio` | JWT issuer |
| `Jwt:Audience` | `RameStudioApp` | JWT audience |
| `Stripe:SecretKey` | `sk_test_...` | Stripe test-mode secret key |
| `Stripe:PublishableKey` | `pk_test_...` | Stripe test-mode publishable key |
| `Stripe:WebhookSecret` | `whsec_...` | Stripe webhook signing secret |
| `FileStorage:RootPath` | `/app/data` | Local file storage root directory |
| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:5000/api` | Frontend API base URL |

Full reference is in `.env.example` at the repository root.

---

## 3. Service Health Checks

### 3.1 API — `/health`

```bash
# From host
curl -s http://localhost:5000/health

# From inside the api container
docker compose exec api curl -s http://localhost:5000/health
```

Expected: HTTP 200 with a JSON body indicating status. If the API is not yet ready, you will get connection refused or HTTP 503.

### 3.2 Frontend

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:5173
```

Expected: HTTP 200 (Vite dev server) or the served static HTML (production build).

### 3.3 Postgres

```bash
# From host
docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres -d rame_studio

# Expected: /var/run/postgresql:5432 - accepting connections
```

### 3.4 Redis

```bash
docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping
```

Expected: `PONG`.

### 3.5 Composite health check (one-liner)

```bash
echo "=== API ==="   && curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:5000/health
echo "=== Frontend ===" && curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://localhost:5173
echo "=== Postgres ===" && docker compose exec -T postgres pg_isready -q -U postgres -d rame_studio && echo "OK" || echo "FAIL"
echo "=== Redis ==="    && docker compose exec -T redis redis-cli ping
```

### 3.6 View container status

```bash
docker compose ps
```

All services should show `running` (or `healthy` if healthchecks are configured in `docker-compose.yml`).

---

## 4. Rollback Procedure

Use this when a new release introduces a regression and you need to return to the previous known-good version.

### 4.1 Rollback application code (no DB change)

```bash
# 1. Identify the previous image tag (check docker images or your registry)
docker images rame-studio-api

# 2. Pin the previous tag in docker-compose.yml or override via environment
export RAME_API_IMAGE=rame-studio-api:<previous-tag>

# 3. Rebuild/recreate with the old image
docker compose pull api   # if using a registry
docker compose up -d api

# 4. Verify health
curl -s http://localhost:5000/health
```

### 4.2 Rollback including database schema

EF Core migrations are forward-only by default. To roll back a schema change:

```bash
# 1. Create a rollback migration (reverts the last migration)
docker compose exec api dotnet ef migrations add Rollback_<name> --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api

# 2. Inspect the generated migration to confirm it reverses the changes
#    (locally, under src/Infrastructure/Migrations/)

# 3. Apply the rollback migration
docker compose exec api dotnet ef database update Rollback_<name> --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api

# 4. Verify the API still starts and /health returns 200
```

### 4.3 Full environment rollback (last resort)

```bash
# Stop current stack
docker compose down

# Restore the previous database backup (see Section 5.2)
# Then restart with the previous image tag
docker compose up -d
```

> **Warning:** `docker compose down -v` destroys all Postgres data. Only use it if you intend to rebuild from scratch.

---

## 5. Incident Response & Recovery

### 5.1 Incident triage checklist

| Symptom | First check | Command |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| API returns 5xx | API logs | `docker compose logs api` |
| API won't start | DB connectivity | `docker compose exec api cat /app/logs/*.log` (if file logging enabled) |
| Frontend blank / not loading | Frontend logs + port 5173 | `docker compose logs frontend` |
| DB connection failures | Postgres readiness | `docker compose exec postgres pg_isready` |
| Redis cache errors | Redis ping | `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping` |
| SignalR hub disconnects | API logs + WebSocket upgrade | `docker compose logs api` |

### 5.2 Database backup & restore

#### Backup

```bash
# Dump the running Postgres database to a file on the host
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U postgres rame_studio > backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).sql

# Verify the dump is non-empty
ls -lh backup_*.sql | tail -1
head -5 backup_*.sql
```

#### Restore

```bash
# 1. Stop the API so no writes occur during restore
docker compose stop api

# 2. Restore the dump into Postgres
cat backup_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.sql | docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U postgres -d rame_studio

# 3. Restart the API
docker compose start api

# 4. Verify health
curl -s http://localhost:5000/health
```

### 5.3 Re-run seed data

Seed data is idempotent (roles and users are created only if missing). Safe to re-run at any time.

```bash
docker compose exec api dotnet run --project src/Api -- SeedData.InitializeAsync
```

If you need a clean reseed (e.g. after a DB restore to an empty schema):

```bash
# 1. Apply migrations first
docker compose exec api dotnet ef database update --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api

# 2. Re-seed
docker compose exec api dotnet run --project src/Api -- SeedData.InitializeAsync
```

### 5.4 Log locations

| Component | Log source | How to view |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| API (.NET) | Container stdout/stderr | `docker compose logs api` |
| API (file logs, if enabled) | `/app/logs/` inside api container | `docker compose exec api ls /app/logs/` |
| Frontend (Vite) | Container stdout/stderr | `docker compose logs frontend` |
| Postgres | Container stdout/stderr | `docker compose logs postgres` |
| Redis | Container stdout/stderr | `docker compose logs redis` |
| Docker Compose | All services | `docker compose logs --tail=100` |

Follow logs in real time:

```bash
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose logs -f --tail=50 postgres
```

### 5.5 Common recovery scenarios

**API unhealthy but Postgres is up**
1. Check API logs: `docker compose logs api`
2. Verify migrations applied: `docker compose exec api dotnet ef migrations list`
3. Restart API: `docker compose restart api`

**Postgres not accepting connections**
1. Check Postgres logs: `docker compose logs postgres`
2. Verify volume is mounted and not full
3. Restart Postgres: `docker compose restart postgres`
4. Wait for `pg_isready` to return OK, then restart API

**Redis down (caching/SignalR backplane degraded)**
1. `docker compose restart redis`
2. Verify: `docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping`
3. Restart API to re-establish connections: `docker compose restart api`

**Seed users missing after restore**
1. Re-run seed: see Section 5.3
2. Verify test accounts can log in (Section 6)

---

## 6. Test Accounts (per role)

Seed data creates the following accounts. All emails are confirmed and usable in local / test environments.

| Role | Email | Password | Purpose |
|------|-------|----------|---------|
| Admin | `admin@rame.test` | `Admin123!` | Full platform access, user management, system configuration |
| Team Member | `team@rame.test` | `Team123!` | Project and design operations, admin-or-team policies |
| Customer | `customer@rame.test` | `Customer123!` | Client-facing portal, package purchases, Stripe test checkout |

### 6.1 Quick login smoke test

```bash
# Obtain a JWT for the admin user (adjust endpoint to match your auth controller)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5000/api/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"admin@rame.test","password":"Admin123!"}'
```

Expected: HTTP 200 with a `token` field. Use the token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` headers for protected endpoints.

### 6.2 Stripe test mode

All Stripe operations use test keys (`sk_test_*`, `pk_test_*`). No real money is moved. Use Stripe test cards (e.g. `4242 4242 4242 4242`) for checkout flows.

---

## 7. Quick Reference Card

```bash
# Start everything
docker compose up -d

# Check health
curl http://localhost:5000/health
curl http://localhost:5173
docker compose exec postgres pg_isready -U postgres
docker compose exec redis redis-cli ping

# Migrate + seed
docker compose exec api dotnet ef database update --project src/Infrastructure --startup-project src/Api
docker compose exec api dotnet run --project src/Api -- SeedData.InitializeAsync

# Logs
docker compose logs -f api
docker compose logs -f postgres

# Backup DB
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U postgres rame_studio > backup.sql

# Stop
docker compose down
```

# Product Brief — Rame Studio

**Project:** rame-studio  
**Slug:** rame-studio  
**Date:** 2026-10-27  
**Owner:** Product Agent  
**Status:** draft  
**Source documents:** docs/plan/PLAN.md (approved v3), docs/design/DESIGN.md (locked), docs/references/REFERENCES.md  
**Scope:** Product requirements, user journeys, and release priorities only. No code changes, no publishing, no spend.

---

## 1. Product vision

Rame Studio is a web design and SEO studio platform that lets customers browse services and packages, place orders, and collaborate with a team through dashboards and real-time chat. Admins manage users, services, packages, orders, invoices, leads, blog, and portfolio. Team members manage their calendar, Kanban tasks, and project work. The platform is bilingual (fa/en, RTL-ready), uses JWT authentication, SignalR chat, and Stripe test-mode payments, built on .NET 10 Clean Architecture backend and React 19 / Vite / Tailwind / Antigravity UI frontend.

---

## 2. User personas

### 2.1 Admin

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Name | Studio Administrator |
| Role | `admin` |
| Goals | Manage the studio business: users, services, packages, orders, invoices, leads, blog, portfolio; oversee team workload; configure platform settings. |
| Pain points | No central overview of orders and leads; manual user and content management; no visibility into team capacity. |
| Devices | Desktop (primary), tablet (secondary) |
| Language | fa / en |

### 2.2 Team member

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Name | Designer / SEO Specialist / Developer |
| Role | `team` |
| Goals | View assigned tasks and calendar, update Kanban task status, chat with customers and admins, log work on projects. |
| Pain points | Tasks scattered across tools; no shared calendar; slow customer communication. |
| Devices | Desktop (primary) |
| Language | fa / en |

### 2.3 Customer

| Attribute | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| Name | Business owner / marketing manager |
| Role | `customer` |
| Goals | Browse services and packages, place orders, track project progress, pay invoices, chat with the studio team. |
| Pain points | Hard to compare service packages; no order status visibility; slow email-only communication. |
| Devices | Desktop and mobile |
| Language | fa / en (RTL for Persian) |

---

## 3. Key user journeys per role

### 3.1 Customer journeys

**J-C1 — Browse and select a service package**
1. Customer lands on the public home page (fa or en).
2. Browses Services and Packages pages.
3. Selects a package and views details.
4. Clicks "Order" / "Get quote".

**J-C2 — Register and place an order**
1. Customer signs up (email + password) or logs in.
2. Completes profile if needed.
3. Adds a package to cart / submits an order request.
4. Proceeds to checkout (Stripe test mode in M3, live later).
5. Receives order confirmation and invoice.

**J-C3 — Track order and chat with the team**
1. Customer opens the Customer Dashboard.
2. Views active projects and order status.
3. Opens Chat to message the studio team (SignalR real-time).
4. Receives replies and updates.

**J-C4 — Manage account and invoices**
1. Customer views Orders and Invoices pages.
2. Downloads invoices, checks payment status.
3. Updates profile and password.

### 3.2 Team member journeys

**J-T1 — Start the day: calendar and tasks**
1. Team member logs in to the Team Dashboard.
2. Views today's calendar events and assigned Kanban cards.
3. Picks a task and moves it to "In Progress".

**J-T2 — Work on a task**
1. Opens Task Detail from Kanban.
2. Updates status, adds notes, logs hours.
3. Moves card to "Review" or "Done".

**J-T3 — Communicate with customers and admin**
1. Opens Chat from the Team area.
2. Replies to customer messages in real time (SignalR).
3. Escalates issues to admin when needed.

**J-T4 — Report progress**
1. Views Reports page for personal/team task completion.
2. Shares status with admin during stand-up.

### 3.3 Admin journeys

**J-A1 — Daily overview**
1. Admin opens the Admin Dashboard.
2. Reviews key metrics: orders, leads, revenue, active users.
3. Checks recent chats and support tickets.

**J-A2 — Manage users and roles**
1. Opens Users page.
2. Creates, edits, or deactivates customer/team/admin accounts.
3. Resets passwords or assigns roles.

**J-A3 — Manage catalog and content**
1. Creates/edits Services, Packages, Portfolio items, Blog posts.
2. Publishes or archives content.
3. Updates pricing and availability.

**J-A4 — Manage orders and invoices**
1. Opens Orders page; reviews new orders.
2. Assigns orders to team members.
3. Generates/sends invoices; tracks payments (Stripe).

**J-A5 — Oversee team and chats**
1. Views Team calendar and Kanban boards.
2. Monitors Chats across customer conversations.
3. Intervenes in customer support when needed.

---

## 4. Feature requirements mapped to PLAN.md milestones

| Feature | Requirement summary | Persona | PLAN.md milestone | PLAN.md reference |
|---------|--------------------|---------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Solution scaffold | .NET 10 Clean Architecture solution (Domain, Application, Infrastructure, API) + React 19/Vite frontend scaffold | All | M1 | T1–T9 |
| Backend infrastructure | EF Core 10 + Npgsql/PostgreSQL, Docker compose, migrations, seed data | All | M1 | T1–T9, T49–T51 |
| Public site + i18n | Home, Services, Packages, Portfolio, About, Blog, Contact; fa/en RTL; Vazirmatn + Inter fonts; Vitrea design tokens; light/dark mode | Customer | M1 | T10–T17 |
| Auth + Identity | JWT auth, ASP.NET Core Identity, login/signup/password reset, role-based access (admin/team/customer) | All | M2 | T18–T25 |
| Customer portal | Customer dashboard, projects, project detail, packages, checkout, orders, invoices, chat | Customer | M3 | T26–T32 |
| Mock checkout | Stripe test-mode payment adapter (IPaymentService + PaymentService) | Customer | M3 | T31 |
| Team area | Calendar, Kanban board, tasks, task detail, reports, chat | Team member | M4 | T33–T36 |
| Real-time chat | SignalR ChatHub + frontend chat components (conversation list, message list, input, unread badge) | All | M5 | T37–T41 |
| File storage | Local file storage service (uploads, invoices, assets) | All | M5 | T41 |
| Admin panel | Admin dashboard, users, services, packages, orders, invoices, leads, blog, portfolio, calendar, tasks, reports, chats | Admin | M6 | T43–T48 |
| Release packaging | Backend + frontend Dockerfiles, docker-compose, wait-for-db + entrypoint scripts, README with build/run/seed/test accounts | All | M7 | T49–T53 |

### Cross-cutting requirements (all milestones)

- **i18n (fa/en, RTL):** react-i18n, fa.json + en.json, RTL CSS overrides, sidebar stays left in RTL.
- **JWT auth:** JWT interceptor on apiClient, useAuth hook, role-based route guards.
- **SignalR chat:** useSignalR hook, real-time message delivery, unread badges.
- **Stripe payments:** test-mode adapter in M3; interface IPaymentService defined in Application layer.
- **Design system:** Vitrea tokens (colors, typography, spacing, radius, shadows), Antigravity UI wrappers, shadcn/ui primitives, light/dark mode toggle.
- **Testing:** xUnit domain/application/infrastructure/API tests + Playwright e2e (signup, login, password reset, chat, checkout).
- **Performance:** Lighthouse 90+ on home page.

---

## 5. Release priorities and milestone ordering

### Milestone order (fixed per PLAN.md)

1. **M1 — Solution scaffold + backend infrastructure** (P0)  
   Foundation: solution structure, database, Docker, public site shell, i18n. Nothing else can start without this.

2. **M2 — Auth + Identity** (P0)  
   JWT authentication and role-based access control. Required before any role-specific dashboard.

3. **M3 — Customer portal + mock checkout** (P1)  
   First customer-facing value: browse, order, pay (Stripe test mode). Revenue path begins here.

4. **M4 — Team area: calendar, Kanban tasks** (P1)  
   Team productivity: calendar, Kanban, tasks, reports. Enables delivery of customer orders.

5. **M5 — Real-time chat + file storage** (P1)  
   SignalR chat connects customer ↔ team ↔ admin; file storage supports invoices and uploads.

6. **M6 — Admin panel** (P2)  
   Business operations: users, catalog, orders, invoices, leads, content. Builds on data created in M3–M5.

7. **M7 — Docker + release** (P0)  
   Production packaging: multi-stage Dockerfiles, compose, entrypoint/seed, README. Blocks deployment.

### Release priority summary

| Priority | Milestones | Rationale |
|----------|------------|-----------|
| P0 (must have, blocks others) | M1, M2, M7 | Foundation, security/auth, deployability |
| P1 (core customer/team value) | M3, M4, M5 | Orders, team delivery, real-time communication |
| P2 (business operations) | M6 | Admin management layer, depends on M3–M5 data |

### Release sequence

**Release 1 (Alpha):** M1 + M2 — scaffold, auth, public site. Internal testing only.  
**Release 2 (Beta):** M3 + M4 — customer orders + team task delivery. Stripe test mode.  
**Release 3 (Beta 2):** M5 — real-time chat + file storage.  
**Release 4 (RC):** M6 — admin panel complete.  
**Release 5 (GA):** M7 — Docker packaging, seed data, README, production-ready release.

---

## 6. Acceptance criteria (from PLAN.md)

- AC-12: Lighthouse score 90+ on home page.
- AC-13: Light/dark mode toggle persists preference.
- E2E tests: password reset, customer signup, chat message send/receive, Stripe test checkout, admin user CRUD.

---

## 7. Out of scope (for this release)

- Live Stripe production keys (test mode only in M3–M7).
- Mobile native apps (responsive web only).
- File storage beyond local disk (S3/Azure Blob later).
- Email notifications beyond password reset (in-app chat is the primary channel).

# SEO Audit — Rame Studio

**Project:** rame-studio
**Slug:** rame-studio
**Date:** 2026-10-27
**Status:** Draft (internal review only — do not publish, do not spend money)
**Owner:** SEO Agent
**Related:** docs/plan/PLAN.md (approved v3, T12–T14 SEO tasks), docs/design/DESIGN.md (locked)

---

## 1. Keyword Research & Search Intent Map

### 1.1 Target market
Rame Studio is a web design & SEO studio serving Persian (fa) and English (en) audiences. Primary service intent: studio-management services (web design, SEO, branding, packages, portfolio). Secondary intent: informational (blog, about, contact).

### 1.2 Keyword clusters

| Cluster | Primary keywords (fa) | Primary keywords (en) | Intent | Priority | Target page |
|---------|----------------------|----------------------|--------|----------|-------------|
| Web design | طراحی وب، طراحی سایت، سایت شرکتی | web design, website design, corporate website | Commercial investigation | High | /services, /packages |
| SEO services | سئو، بهینه‌سازی سایت، سئو فنی | seo services, technical seo, seo audit | Commercial investigation | High | /services |
| Branding | برندینگ، طراحی لوگو، هویت بصری | branding, logo design, brand identity | Commercial investigation | Medium | /services |
| Packages | بسته طراحی سایت، قیمت طراحی سایت | web design packages, website pricing | Transactional | High | /packages |
| Portfolio | نمونه کار، پروژه‌های انجام شده | portfolio, web design portfolio | Commercial investigation | Medium | /portfolio |
| About | درباره ما، رامه استودیو | about us, Rame Studio | Navigational | Medium | /about |
| Blog | آموزش سئو، طراحی وبلاگ | seo tutorial, web design blog | Informational | Medium | /blog |
| Contact | تماس با ما، درخواست قیمت | contact us, request quote | Transactional | High | /contact |

### 1.3 Search intent map

| Intent type | User query pattern | Content format | CTA | Funnel stage |
|-------------|-------------------|----------------|-----|--------------|
| Informational | "سئو چیست؟", "how to design a website" | Blog article, guide | Read more / newsletter | Top |
| Commercial investigation | "بهترین شرکت طراحی وب", "web design pricing comparison" | Services, packages, portfolio | Request quote | Middle |
| Transactional | "سفارش طراحی سایت", "buy web design package" | Checkout, contact form | Buy now / contact | Bottom |
| Navigational | "رامه استودیو", "rame studio login" | Home, login, dashboard | Sign in / explore | Bottom |

### 1.4 Keyword research recommendations
- Use Google Keyword Planner, Ahrefs, or SEMrush (free tiers) to validate search volume for fa/en terms.
- Prioritize long-tail Persian keywords with lower competition (e.g., "طراحی سایت برای استودیو", "seo برای سایت شرکتی").
- Map each keyword to exactly one canonical URL to avoid keyword cannibalization.
- Review quarterly; add new clusters as services expand.

---

## 2. Technical SEO Checklist

### 2.1 Sitemap.xml
- [ ] Generate `sitemap.xml` at root (`/sitemap.xml`) listing all public, indexable URLs.
- [ ] Include only 200-status, canonical URLs; exclude `/admin/*`, `/team/*`, `/customer/*`, `/login`, `/register`.
- [ ] Include `lastmod` (ISO 8601), `changefreq`, and `priority` for each URL.
- [ ] Split into sitemap index if > 50,000 URLs or > 50 MB.
- [ ] Reference sitemap in `robots.txt`.
- [ ] Submit to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

### 2.2 Robots.txt
- [ ] Serve `robots.txt` at root (`/robots.txt`).
- [ ] Disallow admin/customer/team routes and API endpoints.
- [ ] Allow all public pages (`/`, `/services`, `/packages`, `/portfolio`, `/about`, `/blog`, `/contact`).
- [ ] Include `Sitemap:` directive pointing to `sitemap.xml`.
- [ ] Do not use `noindex` in robots.txt (use meta robots tag instead).

### 2.3 Meta tags
- [ ] Unique `<title>` per page (50–60 characters), primary keyword near front.
- [ ] Unique `<meta name="description">` per page (120–160 characters), compelling CTA.
- [ ] `<meta charset="UTF-8">` and `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`.
- [ ] Open Graph tags (`og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`, `og:locale`, `og:type`).
- [ ] Twitter Card tags (`twitter:card`, `twitter:title`, `twitter:description`, `twitter:image`).
- [ ] Canonical `<link rel="canonical">` on every page, self-referencing.
- [ ] `lang` and `dir` attributes on `<html>` (fa/rtl, en/ltr).

### 2.4 JSON-LD structured data
- [ ] Organization schema on homepage and about page.
- [ ] Service schema on services page (one per service).
- [ ] Offer schema on packages page (one per package).
- [ ] BreadcrumbList schema on all content pages.
- [ ] Article/BlogPosting schema on blog articles.
- [ ] Validate with Schema Markup Validator and Rich Results Test.
- [ ] Include `@id` stable identifiers and `sameAs` links to social profiles.

### 2.5 Core Web Vitals
- [ ] LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) ≤ 2.5s (75th percentile, mobile).
- [ ] INP (Interaction to Next Paint) ≤ 200ms (75th percentile, mobile).
- [ ] CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) ≤ 0.1 (75th percentile, mobile).
- [ ] TTFB ≤ 600ms.
- [ ] Optimize images (WebP/AVIF, lazy loading, correct dimensions).
- [ ] Minimize render-blocking CSS/JS; defer non-critical scripts.
- [ ] Enable gzip/brotli compression and HTTP/2.
- [ ] Monitor via PageSpeed Insights and Chrome UX Report (CrUX).

### 2.6 Additional technical items
- [ ] HTTPS enforced (HSTS, redirect HTTP → HTTPS).
- [ ] Clean, descriptive URL structure (no query strings for content pages).
- [ ] 404 page returns 404 status with helpful navigation.
- [ ] 301 redirects for any moved/removed URLs.
- [ ] XML sitemap and robots.txt accessible to crawlers (no auth required).
- [ ] No intrusive interstitials blocking content on mobile.

---

## 3. Structured Data Implementation Verification

### 3.1 Organization (schema.org/Organization)
**Required fields:**
- `@type`: "Organization"
- `name`: "Rame Studio" (fa: "رامه استودیو")
- `url`: canonical homepage URL
- `logo`: URL to logo image
- `sameAs`: social profile URLs
- `address`: PostalAddress (optional, if physical location)
- `contactPoint`: ContactPoint (optional)
- `founder`, `foundingDate`, `areaServed`: ["IR", "US"] (optional)

**Implementation location:** `frontend/src/lib/structured-data.ts` — `organizationData()` helper.
**Verification:** Schema Markup Validator returns 0 errors; Rich Results Test shows Organization eligible.

### 3.2 Service (schema.org/Service)
**Required fields:**
- `@type`: "Service"
- `name`: service name (fa/en)
- `description`: service description
- `provider`: Organization reference (`@id`)
- `serviceType`: category (e.g., "Web Design", "SEO")
- `areaServed`: ["IR", "US"]
- `offers`: Offer reference(s)
- `hasOfferCatalog`: OfferCatalog (optional, for service bundles)

**Implementation location:** `frontend/src/lib/structured-data.ts` — `serviceData()` helper; rendered on `/services`.
**Verification:** Each service card includes JSON-LD; validator passes; no duplicate `@id` for same service.

### 3.3 Offer (schema.org/Offer)
**Required fields:**
- `@type`: "Offer"
- `name`: package/offer name
- `description`: offer description
- `price`: numeric price
- `priceCurrency`: "IRR" or "USD"
- `availability`: "InStock" or "PreOrder"
- `url`: package page URL
- `priceValidUntil`: ISO date (optional)

**Implementation location:** `frontend/src/lib/structured-data.ts` — `offerData()` helper; rendered on `/packages`.
**Verification:** Price matches displayed price; currency correct; availability accurate.

### 3.4 BreadcrumbList (schema.org/BreadcrumbList)
**Required fields:**
- `@type`: "BreadcrumbList"
- `itemListElement`: array of `ListItem` with `position`, `name`, `item` (URL)

**Implementation location:** rendered on all content pages (`/services`, `/packages`, `/portfolio`, `/about`, `/blog`, `/contact`).
**Verification:** Breadcrumb trail matches URL hierarchy; last item is current page (not linked); validator passes.

### 3.5 Article / BlogPosting (schema.org/Article)
**Required fields:**
- `@type`: "Article" or "BlogPosting"
- `headline`: article title
- `author`: Person or Organization reference
- `datePublished`: ISO 8601
- `dateModified`: ISO 8601 (if updated)
- `image`: featured image URL
- `publisher`: Organization reference
- `articleBody`: main content (optional, can be summary)

**Implementation location:** rendered on `/blog` article pages.
**Verification:** Article schema present on each blog post; dates accurate; author linked to Organization.

### 3.6 Verification procedure
1. Run `npm test` (or equivalent) — `tests/seo-structured-data.test.ts` must pass.
2. Paste page URL into Google's Rich Results Test (search.google.com/test/rich-results).
3. Paste JSON-LD into Schema Markup Validator (schema.validator.nu).
4. Confirm no critical errors; warnings acceptable for optional fields.
5. Re-verify after any template or data change.

---

## 4. Multilingual SEO (fa/en RTL)

### 4.1 URL structure
**Recommended:** language subdirectory pattern
```
/fa/          → Persian (default/primary)
/en/          → English
/fa/services  → Persian services
/en/services  → English services
```

**Alternative (if subdirectory not feasible):** subdomain (`fa.ramestudio.com`, `en.ramestudio.com`) or path parameter (`?lang=fa`, `?lang=en`) — not recommended due to canonicalization complexity.

**Decision:** Use `/fa/` and `/en/` subdirectories. Root (`/`) redirects to `/fa/` (Persian is primary market).

### 4.2 Hreflang implementation
**Required on every page:**
```html
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="fa" href="https://ramestudio.com/fa/page" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://ramestudio.com/en/page" />
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://ramestudio.com/fa/page" />
```

**Rules:**
- Each language version references all language versions including itself.
- `x-default` points to the primary (Persian) version for unmatched locales.
- URLs must be absolute (include protocol and domain).
- Hreflang values must be valid BCP 47 (`fa`, `en`).
- No self-referencing hreflang missing; every page must have a complete set.

**Implementation:** React component or middleware injects hreflang tags based on current route and language.

### 4.3 RTL/LTR handling
- `<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">` for Persian pages.
- `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">` for English pages.
- Tailwind CSS supports RTL via `rtl` plugin or logical properties (`margin-inline-start`, `padding-inline-end`, etc.).
- Antigravity UI components must respect `dir` attribute (mirror icons, text alignment, layout direction).
- Font fallback: Persian fonts (Vazirmatn, IranSans) for fa; system/inter for en.
- Ensure numbers, dates, and currency format per locale (fa: Arabic-Indic numerals optional, en: Western).

### 4.4 Content localization
- Translate all visible text; do not machine-translate without human review.
- Meta titles and descriptions must be unique per language (not direct copies).
- Keywords differ per language; perform separate keyword research for fa and en.
- Images with text should be localized or avoided; use CSS text over images.
- Date formats: fa (Persian/Solar Hijri or Gregorian with Persian locale), en (Gregorian).

### 4.5 Canonicalization across languages
- Each language version has its own self-referencing canonical.
- Do not canonicalize `/en/page` to `/fa/page` — they are distinct content.
- Use hreflang (not canonical) to signal language relationships.

### 4.6 Multilingual SEO checklist
- [ ] URL structure: `/fa/` and `/en/` subdirectories implemented.
- [ ] Root redirects to `/fa/`.
- [ ] Hreflang tags present on all pages (fa, en, x-default).
- [ ] `lang` and `dir` attributes correct per language.
- [ ] RTL CSS applied correctly (no layout breakage).
- [ ] Unique meta tags per language.
- [ ] Sitemap includes all language versions.
- [ ] Search Console: separate property or domain property with language filters.
- [ ] No mixed-language content on a single page (fa page fully Persian, en page fully English).

---

## 5. Acceptance Criteria Mapping

| AC | Requirement | Status | Location in AUDIT.md |
|----|-------------|--------|---------------------|
| 1 | Keyword research & search intent map for studio-management services | Defined | Section 1 |
| 2 | Technical SEO checklist (sitemap, robots, meta tags, JSON-LD, Core Web Vitals) | Defined | Section 2 |
| 3 | Structured data implementation verification (Organization, Service, Offer, BreadcrumbList, Article) | Defined | Section 3 |
| 4 | Multilingual SEO for fa/en RTL (hreflang, URL structure) | Defined | Section 4 |

---

## 6. Next Steps (T12–T14)

1. Implement sitemap.xml and robots.txt endpoints (backend).
2. Add JSON-LD structured data helpers and render on pages (frontend).
3. Implement hreflang tags and `/fa/` `/en/` URL structure (frontend + routing).
4. Run structured data tests and validate with Schema Markup Validator.
5. Measure Core Web Vitals via PageSpeed Insights; optimize as needed.
6. Submit sitemap to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.

---
